behavior.text: the table is a constant array in the executable at 0x140681C80 (IDB name tbl_OpeningTaskSteps); its entries are 8 bytes apart and cover ids 0..15.
the table ends at id 15. The next object starts immediately after it at 0x140681D00 and is a different table, tbl_EventSoundGroups; the qword there is not a handler and no dispatch site refers to it.

both scene loops dispatch with tbl_OpeningTaskSteps[dword_1418772E0[dword_141877480 - 1]](), at 0x140331D2D in SceneLoop_Run and 0x14039DE79 in SceneLoop_RunAlt. The id comes from the top of the task stack, not from a direct call.

the handler's first argument is the 100-byte scene frame at unk_1418772F0 + 100 x (depth - 1), where depth is dword_141877480 (rests on the frame writes in OpeningScene_Start; the decompiled dispatch call shows no argument).
only those two sites read the table; a cross-reference scan of 0x140681C80 finds the two dispatch instructions and no writer.

the 16 ids map to: 0 OpeningTask_0, 1 OpeningTask_1, 2 OpeningMenu_Task, 3 OpeningSubmenu_Task, 4 OpeningTask_4, 5 OpeningTask_5, 6 OpeningTask_6, 7 OpeningTask_7, 8 OpeningTask_8, 9 OpeningTask_9, 10 OpeningTask_10, 11 TitleScene_DemoReturn, 12 OpeningTask_12, 13 OpeningScene_Resume, 14 TitleScene_Task, 15 TitleScene_NewGameHandoff.
all 16 entries point at separate function starts.
id 14 is the title scene task. It calls TitleScene_Update and, on the result, replaces the top task id with 15, 13 or 11, or ends the scene with hand-over code 0, 1 or 3.
id 13 is the opening resume task. It sets dword_1418825EC to 0, pops itself and re-enters OpeningScene_Start.

id 4 is the opening text/menu stage, pushed by Opening_LoadMessageSprites. id 0 (OpeningTask_0) is the mode-0 bridge to the title: while g_MovieRequestId is 0 or greater it returns and stays on top; at -1 it clears scene flag bit 1, pops itself and calls TitleScene_Start, which pushes id 14. It never pushes id 1.

id 9 (OpeningTask_9) is the alternate loop's first task: it clears scene flag bit 1 when no movie is requested, sets bit 6, pops itself, requests PSP movie-file row 0x10, writes event id 16 and pushes id 10.

id 10 (OpeningTask_10) waits while g_MovieRequestId is 0 or greater, then fades the UI agent at +400 to state 15, waits for its state 4/1, detaches its add-on and, in the code path, toggles scene flag bit 0. no function stores ids 2, 8 or 12 on the task stack. Ids 2 and 12 are the only handlers that enter the stage chain (id 2 row 0 via Opening_LoadMessageSprites, id 12 accept), so the chain 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 1 and the task-4 shortcut 4 -> 7 are not reached from either scene loop in this build.

the task stack has no visible bound. Every push stores at the current depth and increments it; every pop decrements it (some by more than one). None of the accesses to dword_141877480 compares it with a limit before indexing.
the first 100-byte scene frame used by the dispatch starts at 0x1418772F0; the depth counter dword_141877480 sits at 0x141877480, immediately after the fourth frame.
the only task ids ever stored on the stack are 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15. No store of 2, 8 or 12 was found in any function that accesses the array.
the id array therefore has room for four ids (0x1418772E0..0x1418772EF) before the first scene frame (rests on the array's 4-byte stride and the adjacent frame base).
what the game does if the depth leaves 1..4. Nothing in the code guards an overflow (a fifth id would overwrite the first scene frame) or an underflow (depth 0 reads the dword before the id array).
